articles.title: NFL Panic Meter: Chiefs have to address their offensive issues now, before they regret it
articles.summary: The Chiefs had a rough night in a 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday night.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are 5-1 with only a road loss to the Seattle Seahawks. Overall, they're fine.

Yet, Sunday night had to be an unnerving performance. The Seahawks were the first team to shut down Kenneth Walker III, and the Chiefs offense melted. They had the fewest points (3), yards (213) and first downs (11) in any start over Patrick Mahomes' career, according to NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno.

The Seahawks defense can do that to teams. But for the Chiefs, it renewed the worry about the weapons around Patrick Mahomes. Nobody made plays on Sunday night. Kansas City's leading receiver had 44 yards. And while Walker will not have many games in which he has just 36 rushing yards, he has never been asked to carry an offense over a long season. He had 14.2 carries per game through four seasons with the Seahawks and this season he's at 20. That's a lot of extra carries for a running back over a full season. There has to be concern about putting so much pressure on him over 17 games and then a postseason.

Rashee Rice's absence hurt on Sunday night and when he's able to return from hamstring and knee injuries, maybe everything will look better. Xavier Worthy can drop down from a featured role that he probably can't thrive in, Travis Kelce can be more of a secondary piece at his age as well and others can play in smaller roles. Realistically, even if Rice comes back healthy, the Chiefs probably do need some help.

There aren't a lot of difference-making receivers available at the trade deadline, but there could be some. Jacksonville's Brian Thomas Jr., Cleveland's Jerry Jeudy, Tennessee's Calvin Ridley and Minnesota's Jauan Jennings are among those who could be available. The Chiefs have to look into all possibilities to make sure they're not stuck short on offense late in the season or the playoffs. Right now too much is on Walker's shoulders. It will eventually have to shift back to Mahomes. And he'll need more help.

Panic meter: Nothing too high for a very good team, but they can't ignore needs.

When you start 0-4, you can't afford a big loss. Certainly not one as a 10-point favorite at home.

The Houston Texans are 2-5 after losing in overtime to the New York Giants. It's hard to completely bury them, because the talent is still there. But now a team that couldn't even beat J.J. McCarthy at home has to go 8-2 at least to realistically be in the wild-card hunt. The defense is way worse than anyone was expecting, and the offense isn't good enough to overcome that. If it weren't for the Chargers, this would be the NFL's most disappointing team.

Panic meter: Still a sliver of hope at a rebound, but let's not waste any more time thinking about the 2026 Texans until they're back to .500.

The Panthers trailed 43-6 at home on Sunday to a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team that was 1-5 coming in. Even if anyone was wondering if the Panthers were playing over their heads at 3-2, nobody expected that.

The score was 33-6 at halftime and everything was bad.

"I mean, it's a shock," Panthers coach Dave Canales told the media after the game . "For me to be able to move on from it, because I've literally never been a part of a half of football like that. To experience it in all phases: blocked kick, sack-fumble, interception, blocked punt and the defensive side not getting off the field in different ways. It was so crazy and so egregiously different than the ball we're used to playing."

No matter how bad the game was, the Panthers are allowed one ugly loss. They had looked good during a 3-2 start, particularly Bryce Young having a breakout season at quarterback. But next up is a game at the Packers and then a home game against the Broncos. We're about to find out if Carolina has staying power.

Panic meter: The Panthers are on notice after whatever that was on Sunday.

It was a bit strange for Saints owner Gayle Benson to seemingly put coach Kellen Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis on notice last week, saying she will "not accept this level of performance," according to the Associated Press. The Saints were seemingly on the right track late last season, although they were off to a 2-4 start this season. Then they had an ugly 16-10 loss in Paris to the Steelers, which can't help anything.

"Mrs. B's great," Moore said last week according to the AP , before facing the Steelers. "We all want better results, and that's how this business is."

The thought of Moore being in any trouble after a good finish to last season, his first as coach of the Saints, was far from anyone's mind. Until Benson sounded upset at the way the season is going. Then it got worse.

Panic meter: Probably nothing to worry about yet, but Moore might want to quickly win some games just in case.

The Ravens have a very talented team and are no longer better than 50% to make the playoffs, according to DVOA .

The Ravens' odds dipped to 41.4% via DVOA after a bad loss to the Bengals in which they were outscored 35-0 in the second half. The problem is the Ravens face the toughest remaining schedule in the NFL, via DVOA. Lamar Jackson didn't return last week from an ankle injury and that's becoming a point of contention. The Ravens simply need him back if they're going to survive a rough schedule, and that includes their next two games against the Bills and Jaguars. For a 4-3 team, there should be a lot of concern in Baltimore. And if this season ends up with no playoff berth, who knows what changes might come next.

Panic meter: With Jackson back, maybe it will be OK. If he doesn't return soon, the season is probably headed downhill fast.

articles.title: How Jets' 2027 NFL Draft Pick Is Impacted By Colts' Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner Trades
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts sent shockwaves across the NFL when they traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday, and the impact was also felt on the East Coast.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts sent shockwaves across the NFL when they traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday, and the impact was also felt on the East Coast.

ESPN's Field Yates pointed out that the New York Jets are the "sneaky winner" of Tuesday's trade between the Colts and the Seahawks because they own Indianapolis' 2027 first-round draft pick.

At 2-5, the Colts appear to be committing to a rebuild after trading Nelson, who has been selected to the Pro Bowl in each of his first eight NFL seasons, and Buckner, a three-time Pro Bowler himself. Yates noted that Tuesday's Nelson deal "could be the first of multiple trades the Colts make for their quality veteran players as they look towards the future."

As it turns out, it wasn't long before Buckner was on the move as well.

The Jets acquired two first-round picks from the Colts as part of the 2025 trade for star cornerback Sauce Gardner. At the time, Indianapolis appeared to be one of the top Super Bowl contenders in the AFC, facilitating the decision to make an all-in move. Unfortunately, the team bottomed out and failed to make the playoffs.

In addition to the Colts' first-round pick, the Jets will also have the better first-round selection from the Dallas Cowboys or Green Bay Packers following the trade that sent defensive tackle Quinnen Williams to Dallas. With three first-round selections, New York is expected to finally add its franchise quarterback while also addressing other needs with blue-chip prospects.

Jets fans will be rooting for the Colts to continue tearing things down before the Nov. 10 trade deadline and tank the rest of the season, as New York could end up with multiple top-10 picks in the 2027 draft.

articles.title: Should the Eagles Turn to Joe Milton After Another Disappointing Loss?
articles.summary: Joe Milton could be the next quarterback to get an opportunity with the Philadelphia Eagles as the team searches for answers during a difficult stretch of th...
articles.body:
Joe Milton could be the next quarterback to get an opportunity with the Philadelphia Eagles as the team searches for answers during a difficult stretch of the 2026 NFL season.

Philadelphia suffered another disappointing loss Monday night, falling 38-21 to the Dallas Cowboys. Tanner McKee started in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, but the Eagles could not maintain their momentum after briefly taking the lead in the third quarter.

With the team dropping five consecutive games, questions are beginning to emerge about whether Philadelphia should give Milton a chance to lead the offense.

McKee Has Not Done Enough to Silence Questions

McKee entered the starting role with an opportunity to prove he could keep the Eagles competitive while Hurts recovers. However, Philadelphia has struggled to find consistency on offense, and Monday's loss added to the frustration.

McKee finished with 211 passing yards, one touchdown and one interception against Dallas. Although he showed some positive moments, the Eagles ultimately struggled to keep pace with the Cowboys in the second half.

The difficult circumstances surrounding McKee should not be ignored. He has limited starting experience and was not originally expected to carry the offense for an extended period. Still, Philadelphia needs better results if it hopes to turn its season around.

Milton offers something different. The former Tennessee Volunteers quarterback possesses tremendous arm strength and athletic ability, giving the Eagles a potential option to stretch the field and create plays outside the pocket.

Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad after Hurts was sidelined. While Milton has appeared in NFL games, he remains relatively inexperienced and has yet to establish himself as a reliable starter.

His physical tools could make him an intriguing option, especially if the Eagles believe the offense needs a different approach. However, arm strength alone does not guarantee success. Milton would need to demonstrate that he can make smart decisions, protect the football and operate the offense consistently.

The Eagles should seriously consider giving Milton an opportunity if McKee continues to struggle. With the team searching for answers, evaluating another quarterback could provide valuable information about its options moving forward.

However, Milton should not automatically receive the starting job simply because he has more exciting physical tools.

Philadelphia should evaluate both quarterbacks in practice and determine who gives the offense the best chance to succeed. If McKee cannot deliver improved results, turning to Milton could be a worthwhile gamble.

The Eagles need a spark, and Milton may be worth a look.

articles.title: Seahawks Trade: Quenton Nelson Deal Casts Doubt on Jonathan Taylor Pursuit
articles.summary: Seattle landed eight-time Pro Bowler Quenton Nelson, but the trade raises new questions about the Seahawks' reported interest in Colts running back Jonathan...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks have made their blockbuster trade with the Indianapolis Colts. It just wasn't the one many fans expected.

Seattle agreed to acquire eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson on Tuesday, Oct. 27, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. The Seahawks are sending a 2027 third-round draft pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection to Indianapolis in exchange for the veteran offensive lineman.

The acquisition provides a significant upgrade to Seattle's offensive line, but it also raises questions about the team's reported pursuit of Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.

Seattle was among four teams connected to Taylor in a report published Sunday. Now, general manager John Schneider has spent another premium draft pick to address a different position, while two of the Seahawks' existing running backs are approaching potential returns from injuries.

Seahawks Trade Reduces Draft Capital for Jonathan Taylor Pursuit

Schefter and Rapoport reported Oct. 25 that the Seahawks, Green Bay Packers , Denver Broncos and Minnesota Vikings were among the teams that had considered, or were expected to consider, a trade for Taylor.

However, Indianapolis reportedly has a high asking price for the 27-year-old running back, who signed a two-year, $44 million contract extension in August.

Seattle's decision to acquire Nelson doesn't eliminate the possibility of another deal, but it changes the equation.

According to Schefter, the Seahawks are sending their 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round selection to Indianapolis for Nelson. That further reduces a collection of future draft picks Schneider had already tapped into.

Seattle previously traded its 2027 fourth-round selection to the Cleveland Browns during the 2026 NFL draft to acquire the pick used on offensive lineman Beau Stephens. The Seahawks subsequently sent their 2027 sixth-round selection to the Los Angeles Chargers in August in exchange for cornerback Avery Smith.

With the Nelson deal, Seattle has now traded away three of its original seven selections in the 2027 draft. The Seahawks retain their original first-, second-, fifth- and seventh-round picks.

Seattle is also projected to receive four compensatory selections in 2027, including one fourth-rounder and three fifth-rounders, according to NFL.com. Those selections have not yet been officially awarded.

Schneider has a lengthy history of making aggressive in-season acquisitions. Seattle obtained Leonard Williams from the New York Giants in 2023, Ernest Jones IV from the Tennessee Titans in 2024 and Rashid Shaheed from the New Orleans Saints in 2025.

The Nelson deal continues that pattern. However, adding Taylor would require Seattle to sacrifice additional draft capital and take on another substantial contract.

Nelson's arrival also gives the Seahawks flexibility along their offensive line. Schefter reported that the acquisition could allow former first-round pick Gray Zabel to move to the right side, where he played in college.

Rather than spending heavily on another running back, Schneider has strengthened the offensive line that will block for whoever is carrying the football.

Seahawks Have Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price Nearing Returns

The Seahawks' running back situation has been complicated by injuries, but reinforcements could arrive before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline.

Veteran Zach Charbonnet has not played this season after suffering a torn ACL during Seattle's playoff victory over the San Francisco 49ers in January.

However, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday, Oct. 26, that Charbonnet would continue practicing in a full capacity this week as the team evaluates his progress.

Macdonald emphasized the importance of managing Charbonnet's recovery, given that he is approximately nine months removed from surgery. Seattle has not committed to a specific return date.

Rookie Jadarian Price is also working toward a return. The Seahawks selected the Notre Dame running back with the No. 32 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, making a substantial investment in the position following Kenneth Walker III's departure in free agency.

Price has been sidelined by a chest injury but is eligible to return from injured reserve. Macdonald indicated Monday that the plan is for Price to resume practicing this week, although his availability for Seattle's upcoming game against the Chicago Bears remains uncertain.

Neither running back is guaranteed to return immediately. Still, getting both healthy would leave the Seahawks with two viable options at a position where they have already invested significant resources.

That makes the Nelson acquisition especially consequential.

Seattle has addressed a weakness along its offensive line without committing another expensive contract to the backfield. The deal also provides an opportunity to improve the running game regardless of which player starts.

Meanwhile, the Colts' willingness to trade Nelson demonstrates that Indianapolis is prepared to move established veterans in exchange for future assets.

That could increase speculation surrounding Taylor before the deadline, even if Seattle is now a less logical destination.

The Seahawks still have the resources to make another move. Whether they're willing to spend them on a position that could soon have two healthy contributors is another question.

articles.title: “You are here”: Tom Brady shares a cryptic message amid reports of new romance with Candice Swanepoel
articles.summary: Tom Brady has fans talking after sharing a deep message about life on his Instagram Story amid rumors linking him to Victoria’s Secret model Candice
articles.body: Tom Brady has fans talking after sharing a deep message about life on his Instagram Story amid rumors linking him to Victoria’s Secret model Candice Swanepoel. The former NFL quarterback shared a famous quote from astronomer Carl Sagan, along with an image of Earth taken by NASA’s Voyager 1 spacecraft in 1990. The picture shows just how tiny our planet looks from space, and the message that comes with it makes you think about life a little differently.Tom Brady turns to a deep Carl Sagan quote as Candice Swanepoel romance reports make headlinesIt goes on to talk about how everyone who has ever lived, loved, fought, or made history has called this tiny planet home. From kings and ordinary people to parents, children, heroes, and even villains, everyone has shared the same little corner of the universe.“Look again at that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us,” the quote begins.The message ends by describing Earth as “a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam.”Brady did not add any words of his own to explain the post. He simply shared the quote, leaving fans to take in its message. But with his personal life making headlines lately, the timing of the Story is certainly interesting.Brady has recently been linked to Candice Swanepoel, the South African model best known for her work with Victoria’s Secret. Reports have suggested that the two have been dating for several months, putting their rumored romance in the spotlight. Even after stepping away from the NFL, Brady continues to draw plenty of attention, whether it is about his football career, family life, or who he might be dating.However, neither Brady nor Swanepoel has publicly confirmed the relationship. For now, the reports remain unconfirmed, and there is no clear picture of where things stand between them.Sagan’s famous “Pale Blue Dot” quote is all about looking at life from a bigger perspective. When Earth is seen from millions of miles away, all the things that seem so important to us suddenly look very small.The message reminds people that, despite their differences, everyone shares the same planet. It touches on everything from love and happiness to struggles, conflicts, and the moments that make up our lives.For now, his post leaves more room for thought than answers. While the dating rumors continue to circulate, Brady has chosen to share a reminder about just how small we all are in the grand scheme of things.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2012, Peyton Manning bought a Denver estate for $4.6 million; in 2023, he added a nearby $5.3 million property
articles.summary: Peyton Manning’s real estate ties to Colorado go back to the year he joined the Denver Broncos.
articles.body: Peyton Manning’s real estate ties to Colorado go back to the year he joined the Denver Broncos. In July 2012, the former quarterback bought a large home in Cherry Hills Village for $4.575 million. More than 11 years later, a company linked to Manning purchased another property nearby for $5.3 million. The two reported purchase prices come to $9.875 million, or roughly $9.9 million combined. County property records document the later transaction, while a report from BusinessDen said the second purchase was intended for business rather than personal use.Manning retired from the NFL in 2016, but he has continued to maintain ties to Colorado. His years with the Broncos included a Super Bowl title, and his family also established a life in the Denver area. The two purchases show the scale of his reported property investment in the state, although the original prices do not tell us what either property is worth today. How Manning's two confirmed Colorado acquisitions total $9.9 million in reported purchase pricesManning bought his Cherry Hills Village mansion in July 2012, shortly after signing with Denver. According to reporting by The Denver Post at the time, he paid $4,575,000 for the home. The property sits on 3.37 acres and measures about 16,000 square feet. It was listed for $5.25 million when it first went on the market in March 2011, meaning Manning bought it below its original asking price. Multiple outlets, including NFL.com and CBS Sports, reported the purchase shortly after it happened.The two-story house has seven bedrooms and several rooms designed for entertaining and family use. Reports on the property have listed features including a media room, a billiards room, an elevator and a safe room. The estate also has extensive outdoor space and a seven-car heated garage. Other reported features include a wine cellar, fireplaces and a heated kennel for dogs. The home’s size and facilities made it a substantial residence for Manning, his wife Ashley and their twin sons.The purchase came during a major change in Manning’s football career. He had spent his first 13 NFL seasons with the Indianapolis Colts, but missed the 2011 season after undergoing multiple neck surgeries. The Colts released him in March 2012, and he signed a five-year contract with the Broncos later that month. The deal was reported at $96 million. Buying a home in Cherry Hills Village gave him a base in the Denver area as he began the next stage of his career.Manning’s second reported Colorado acquisition came in September 2023. Arapahoe County property records show that Wahoo Properties LLC bought a 3,582-square-foot home in the 3900 block of South Colorado Boulevard from the Beverly A. Clark Living Trust on September 20. The reported purchase price was $5.3 million. The property is near Manning’s Cherry Hills Village mansion, according to BusinessDen’s report on the transaction.Both purchases were made through Wahoo Properties LLC, which links the two transactions in public reporting. BusinessDen reported that the company is an Indiana corporation and that Pey Dirt Inc., an Ohio company also doing business as Peyton Manning Inc., is listed as its registered agent. The records establish the company’s purchases and the reported prices, but they do not by themselves confirm the properties’ current market values or Manning’s overall real estate wealth.Adding the reported prices gives a total of $9.875 million: $4.575 million for the 2012 mansion and $5.3 million for the 2023 home. That is commonly rounded to $9.9 million. It is important to describe this as the combined purchase price, not a current valuation. Property values can change over time, and the available reports do not establish what either house might sell for now. Why the retired NFL star's second Denver property was reportedly intended for business useThe second purchase drew attention because the home sits close to Manning’s long-established residence, but reports suggested it was not meant to become another family home. BusinessDen cited a source close to Manning who said the purchase was a business transaction rather than a personal one. According to that source, Manning did not plan to move into the house or demolish it to build a larger mansion beside his existing property.That explanation has to remain attributed to the source. Manning has not been quoted in the report publicly explaining the purpose of the purchase, and the available property records do not state how the house would be used. The records identify the buyer as Wahoo Properties LLC and document the September 2023 transaction. The business-use description comes from the reporting around the sale, not from a recorded statement in the deed.There is also limited public information about the second property’s interior or facilities. The reported size is 3,582 square feet, much smaller than the roughly 16,000-square-foot mansion Manning bought in 2012. Beyond the address area, square footage, seller and purchase price, the reporting does not offer a detailed breakdown of the home’s layout or condition. It would therefore be premature to assume that Manning planned a particular office, commercial operation or redevelopment project there.Manning’s connection to Colorado continued after his playing career ended. He spent the final four seasons of his NFL career with the Broncos and helped the team win Super Bowl 50 in February 2016. He announced his retirement the following month. A 2022 interview cited by the Indianapolis Star also reported that Manning had said his children attended school in the Denver area and that he and Ashley had made Colorado their home.The second purchase adds another reported property to that Colorado story, but it does not establish that Manning planned to move or expand his residence. The clearest details remain the public transaction records and the account from a source close to him. Together, the two purchases total nearly $9.9 million in reported prices, while the reason for the 2023 acquisition remains a reported business purpose rather than a publicly detailed plan.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Seahawks release veteran player after trade on Tuesday
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have made a roster decision following their Quenton Nelson trade.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks made a major addition to their offensive line on Tuesday, acquiring eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson from the Indianapolis Colts . The trade gives Seattle an experienced interior blocker as it looks to improve its offense during the second half of the season.

However, bringing Nelson to Seattle has also forced the Seahawks to make a roster adjustment. With a new guard joining the offensive line, the team has decided to move on from one of its younger players, creating a fresh opportunity for the incoming veteran to strengthen the unit.

The Seahawks waived guard Christian Haynes to make room for Nelson on their 53-man roster (h/t ESPN's Adam Schefter).

Seattle selected Haynes in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, with the 81st overall pick, after his college career at UConn.

Haynes' departure comes as Seattle looks to address its interior offensive line. The team had rotated Haynes and rookie Beau Stephens at right guard earlier in the season while Anthony Bradford was sidelined on injured reserve.

The waiver process allows another NFL team to claim Haynes and take over his contract. If no team claims him, he can become a free agent and explore other opportunities.

What Quenton Nelson brings to the Seahawks

Nelson was selected sixth overall by the Colts in the 2018 NFL Draft and quickly established himself as one of the league's leading offensive guards. He has earned eight Pro Bowl selections and three first-team All-Pro honors, making him a significant addition for Seattle.

The Seahawks sent Indianapolis a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick in exchange for Nelson.

The move also addresses an area Seattle has struggled with this season. The Seahawks ranked 21st in pass-block win rate and 27th in run-block win rate. Nelson's experience in both phases could help improve the team's interior blocking and provide better protection for quarterback Sam Darnold.

articles.title: Colts reportedly trade DT DeForest Buckner to 49ers
articles.summary: The 32-year-old Buckner is set to become a free agent in the offseason.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts continued moving assets out on Tuesday, trading defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick, NFL Insider Tom Pelissero reports.

Buckner returns to a 49ers team that selected him with the No. 7 pick in the 2016 NFL Draft.

A two-time All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowler, Buckner was traded to the Colts in March 2020 after four seasons with the 49ers. In 95 career games in Indianapolis, he recorded 63 total tackles and 47 sacks.

After moving guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks earlier Tuesday, Colts interim general manager Ed Dodds is stockpiling draft picks in order to rebuild the roster. A 2-5 record and three straight losses have put the organization in a position to wave the white flag and look towards 2027.

Buckner expressed his frustration with the Colts' lack of success this season following the Week 7 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. That came a week after saying , "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," after losing to the previously winless Tennessee Titans.

The 32-year-old Buckner is in the final year of his contract and, after receiving a $10 million roster bonus in March, is still owed a little under $8 million for the rest of the season. He carries a $26.6 million salary cap hit, which will leave $10.8 million in dead money on the Colts' books, according to Over the Cap .

If he wasn't moved before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, he was all but certain to leave in free agency.

articles.title: Colts trade veteran G Quenton Nelson to Seahawks for 2 draft picks
articles.summary: Quenton Nelson, 30, is considered one of the league's best offensive linemen.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts had a busy day on Tuesday.

The team announced on Tuesday afternoon that they traded veteran guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks.

In return, Seattle is sending Indianapolis a 2027 third-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported that the Green Bay Packers, Chicago Bears, and Philadelphia Eagles were also interested in Nelson.

Then a few hours later, the Colts reached a deal to send defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers.

Nelson is in the final year of his current deal. He signed a four-year, $80 million extension to remain with the Colts ahead of the 2022 season. Seattle will pay the remaining $9.777 million he is owed, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

Indianapolis selected the guard with the sixth overall pick in the 2018 NFL Draft. Nelson has been named to the Pro Bowl in all eight of his seasons. He has also been a three-time First-Team All-Pro and has missed just four career games.

If Seattle doesn't sign the guard to an extension, he would net the Seahawks a 2028 compensatory draft pick if he leaves in free agency. Speaking of compensatory picks, the Seahawks are expected to already get an extra 2027 third-round pick for Nolan Teasley, who left to become the Vikings' new general manager.

Seattle is also expected to receive comp picks for Kenneth Walker III, Tariq Woolen, Coby Bryant and Boye Mafe, who left in free agency this past offseason.

Nelson's trade isn't a shock, as Indianapolis is projected to undergo a fire sale ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline. His expiring contract made it more likely he'd be moved.

The Colts fired former general manager Chris Ballard on Oct. 19 and started the season 2-5. Indianapolis was a buyer at last year's deadline, acquiring cornerback Sauce Gardner from the New York Jets for two first-round picks and wide receiver AD Mitchell.

Now, a year later, Indy is backtracking and is trying to acquire assets. Moving both Nelson and Buckner on Tuesday is a good start.

The Colts were also "actively shopping" the three-time Pro Bowler prior to the swap, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz .

As for the 49ers, they hold the No. 1 spot in the NFC West standings with a 6-1 record this year.

Still, San Francisco only ranks No. 20 among all teams with 15 total sacks in 2026 and should boast an improved interior pass rush following the addition of Buckner.

In his first seven games this season, he racked up 31 tackles, eight quarterback hits, four sacks and three passes defended. Buckner has also amassed 20 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus .

The veteran has consistently been productive with Indianapolis, recording 26.5 sacks over the prior four years combined.

Buckner will have some time to get acclimated to his new teammates during the 49ers' Week 8 bye before they're set to face the Las Vegas Raiders on Nov. 8.

articles.title: Khalil Mack, Josh Sweat's Top NFL Landing Spots After Colts Trade DeForest Buckner to 49ers
articles.summary: Let the defensive linemen bidding wars begin.
articles.body:
Let the defensive linemen bidding wars begin.

The Indianapolis Colts kicked off the potential run of high-profile trades involving defensive linemen ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline on Tuesday by sending DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

San Francisco landing one of the year's biggest trade pieces means other teams in need of defensive linemen will have to turn their attention elsewhere.

Enter Khalil Mack or Josh Sweat, who could end up on the following teams:

Mack being traded would be anything but a surprise. The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-6, and he is playing on the final year of his deal. If there is a chance he could end up elsewhere next season regardless, Los Angeles would be wise to get whatever it could in return via a trade.

There has already been plenty of speculation about his immediate future, and the Buckner trade only figures to increase the buzz.

As for Sweat, he is signed through 2028 but is on an Arizona Cardinals team that is still in rebuilding mode. Moving him for draft capital could accelerate that rebuilding process, especially since they may not be realistic Super Bowl contenders while he is under contract.

Sweat has also appeared in rumors leading up to the deadline.

The Bears, Bills and Packers all make sense as potential destinations for either player, as they are all contenders in the early going this season that need help along the defensive line.

There is familiarity in place with Mack for Chicago, as he played four seasons for the NFC North team. One of those seasons was 2018 when he finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting.

Chicago has the offensive firepower to challenge for a Super Bowl title, but it needs to make strides on the defensive side to take that next step.

And trading for either Mack or Sweat would be an important step.

As for the Bills, they are an ugly 30th in the league in points allowed per game. They are still 5-1 thanks in large part to Josh Allen's individual brilliance, but the defense will eventually undercut their Lombardi Trophy pursuit without significant improvement.

Green Bay is in a position of need along the defensive line in large part because of injuries.

It lost Javon Hargrave for the season to a torn Achilles , while Micah Parsons is yet to play through the first seven games as he recovers from a torn ACL that cut his 2025 season short.

There is still not an exact timeline on Parsons' return, so Mack or Sweat could help make up for his absence in the meantime.

And then they could form quite a dynamic duo when Parsons does return.

articles.title: 49ers, Colts' Updated Salary Caps, NFL Draft Picks, Depth Charts After DeForest Buckner Trade
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are clearing out salary and stocking up on draft picks after a 2-5 start to the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are clearing out salary and stocking up on draft picks after a 2-5 start to the 2026 season.

The Colts traded star defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick.

Indianapolis also acquired a 2027 third-rounder and 2028 fifth-rounder in exchange for guard Quenton Nelson.

The Colts are now projected to have 10 picks from the second round of the 2027 draft onward, per Spotrac.

The 49ers are projected to hold six 2027 picks, including their own first-rounder, per the AP's Josh Dubow.

The Colts cleared out $17.6 million in salary by trading Buckner and Nelson, according to Spotrac .

Indianapolis now has the most salary cap space in the NFL with $37 million remaining this season, and the fifth-most for 2027 with $97 million in space, according to Spotrac.

Buckner's contract carries a $7.9 million cap hit this season, per Spotrac . The 49ers are currently projected by Spotrac to rank 27th in the NFL with $1.1 million in top 51 cap space.

Buckner could now join a stacked Niners defensive line also featuring Nick bosa, Keion White and Osa Odighizuwa.

The 49ers have been struggling with defensive line depth since losing defensive tackles C.J. West, Alfred Collins and James Thompson Jr. to injury. Defensive ends Nick Bosa and Sam Okuayinonu have also missed time due to injury.

The 49ers have ranked 19th and 20th in the NFL in pass rush win rate and run stop win rate, respectively, so far this season, per ESPN .

Buckner recorded 4.0 sacks in seven games with the Colts, more than any current member of the 49ers defense (White leads the group with 3.5 sacks).

The Niners will hope adding Buckner and bringing back Bosa from injury will help Raheem Morris' unit put together a stronger defensive performance down the stretch.

The Colts likely aren't done selling off players after remaining on for a sixth straight missed postseason.

All eyes will now be on running back Jonathan Taylor and wide receiver Josh Downs ahead of the Nov. 10 deadline.

ESPN's Jordan Raanan previously reported the Colts want at least a second-round pick for Taylor, who is signed through 2028. Downs is playing on an expiring contract but could still draw interest from wide-receiver needy teams looking to make the playoffs.

The Colts began their fire sale by dismissing former general manager Chris Ballard. Interim GM Ed Dodds and owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon could hope stocking up on draft picks will set up the franchise's next general manager for success this spring.

Ballard's successor might not be the only person who could benefit from the Colts selling at the deadline. The New York Jets, which hold the Colts' first-round pick as well as their own and the Dallas Cowboys', will be rooting for the Colts to keep losing down the stretch of the season.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs' Top NFL Landing Spots After Colts Trade Quenton Nelson, Buckner
articles.summary: The fire sale has begun.
articles.body:
The 2-5 Indianapolis Colts traded guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers on Tuesday, a clear response to the team's recent three-game losing streak.

Running back Jonathan Taylor and wideout Josh Downs could be among the other players to find new homes before the Tuesday, Nov. 10 trade deadline. Below, we'll break down some potential destinations for each player.

Yes, the New York Giants seemed to hand the reins back to Cam Skattebo this past week and, yes, he responded with 124 yards on the ground and a touchdown. But he has undeniable speed limitations, and Taylor would be a pretty sizable upgrade.

The 4-2-1 Giants have a real chance to win the NFC East this season, buoyed by the surprisingly strong play of JJ McCarthy, the dynamic Malik Nabers at wideout and a talent-loaded front seven on defense. Taylor would give them a home-run threat in the backfield and would erase some of the residual pain from Saquon Barkley leaving in free agency ahead of the 2024 season and promptly winning a Super Bowl with the Philadelphia Eagles.

Taylor would be a great fit in New York's offense and give the team another elite playmaker. It's a win-now move for a young and ascending team, but the Giants have a real window this season they shouldn't let slip away.

Yes, the Vikings have the veteran pair of Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. But who would you rather have, that duo or Taylor?

The Vikings have not been inspiring on offense and are currently 6-0 largely due to their defense and special teams. Adding an elite option like Taylor in the backfield would give them another dimension as they look to prove that this season's fast start isn't a fluke.

Rhamondre Stevenson has been known to leave some meat on the bone (alongside his fumbling issues) and the New England coaching staff doesn't seem to trust the explosive TreVeyon Henderson. Taylor would certainly provide an immediate upgrade for a team very much in contention mode.

This feels a bit less likely given some of the team's previously splashy moves, like trading for A.J. Brown, but it certainly would make them far scarier as they seek a return to the Super Bowl.

Rashee Rice hasn't been healthy, Tyquan Thornton is likely on injured reserve until late in the regular season or the playoffs and Xavier Worthy simply isn't a No. 1 option at receiver—the Kansas City Chiefs could use some help for Patrick Mahomes.

Downs isn't an elite receiver by any means, but he'd be a nice fit for a Chiefs team in need of help at the position. This is a match that makes a lot of sense.

The Pittsburgh Steelers have a No. 1 option in DK Metcalf and a burgeoning playmaker in Germie Bernard, but adding another threat out wide for Aaron Rodgers would make sense.

The AFC North is wide open at the moment—all four teams are separated by just one game in the standings—and improving on the margins would make a lot of sense for the Steelers.

articles.title: "Wanted to make it bigger for more kids": Travis Kelce’s heartfelt gesture helped feed 25,000 meals to children while keeping the Operation Breakthrough founder’s dream alive
articles.summary: In 2024, Travis Kelce showed how a small act of generosity can make a lasting difference in a community.
articles.body: In 2024, Travis Kelce showed how a small act of generosity can make a lasting difference in a community. The Kansas City Chiefs star teamed up with breakfast brand Kodiak to provide 25,000 meals to children at Operation Breakthrough, a nonprofit serving families in Kansas City. The donation arrived at a meaningful time for the organisation, which was mourning the loss of co-founder Sister Berta. Beyond helping feed children, Kelce’s contribution supported a mission built on compassion, education and the belief that every child deserves a chance to thrive.How Travis Kelce’s donation supported Operation BreakthroughKelce’s partnership with Kodiak brought practical help to children who rely on Operation Breakthrough for essential services. The organisation supports more than 700 children every day, offering resources designed to help them and their families build better futures.The donation also gave the centre a reason to celebrate. Staff prepared a special pancake breakfast featuring Chiefs-themed and Operation Breakthrough-inspired designs, bringing together the football star’s generosity and the nonprofit’s community spirit.For Kelce, whose public profile extends far beyond the football field, the initiative offered a way to connect his success with a cause close to the Kansas City community. Food donations can meet an immediate need, but they can also help raise awareness of organisations working to support children throughout the year.Entrepreneurship educator Shirl Nichols highlighted the importance of keeping generosity at the heart of success.“No matter how big you make it, giving back is your number one priority,” entrepreneurship educator Shirl Nichols said.That message reflects the wider role that athletes and businesses can play when they use their influence to support local organisations. A single donation cannot solve every challenge facing families, but it can provide meaningful assistance while encouraging others to contribute.Operation Breakthrough carries forward Sister Berta’s legacySister Berta and her close friend, Sister Corita, founded Operation Breakthrough in 1971. What began as an effort to care for a few children in a home grew into an organisation serving hundreds of children daily.Sister Berta’s death left a deep emotional mark on the people connected to the nonprofit. Her daughter, Vanshay Purnell, described how her mother’s values continue to guide the organisation’s work.“When I walk in the building, I just feel her," Vanshay Purnell, Sister Berta's daughter, said. "I always think, 'What would Sister Berta or Sister Corita do?' That’s how I usually go through my day-to-day.”Purnell also explained why the founders’ original vision remains important.“They (Sister Berta and Sister Corita) wanted to make it bigger for more kids and more families," Purnell said. "I feel like they’re doing that.”The 25,000-meal donation became part of that continuing effort, linking Kelce’s community support with the founders’ long-standing commitment to children and families.Reflecting on her mother’s impact, Purnell added, “I think she would just be speechless," Purnell said of her mom. "She would be in awe about all the kids they’re helping still. It’s been a long time coming.”For Operation Breakthrough, the donation represented more than a breakfast celebration. It helped sustain a mission that has continued for decades, keeping Sister Berta’s legacy alive through the children and families the organisation serves.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Montez Sweat Apologizes for 'Surprise' PED Suspension Ahead of Return to Bears
articles.summary: Montez Sweat is back for the Chicago Bears, but he is sorry he was suspended for two games after failing a performance-enhancing drug test.
articles.body:
Montez Sweat is back for the Chicago Bears, but he is sorry he was suspended for two games after failing a performance-enhancing drug test.

"I just want to apologize to my teammates, the fan base, everybody, but I'm moving forward now," the pass-rusher said Tuesday, per the Associated Press . He also said the suspension "was a surprise, but you take a lick on the chin and keep moving forward."

Fortunately for Sweat, the Bears defeated the Atlanta Falcons and New England Patriots while he was sidelined.

They mixed in a number of blitzes to account for his absence, and cornerback Kyler Gordon notched four combined sacks in the two games.

Still, the defense will be much better with its veteran pass-rusher back for Monday's game against the Seattle Seahawks. And he is happy to return after being away from the team for multiple weeks.

"It was devastating," Sweat said. "I'm just happy to be back in the building with my teammates. I think that's what I missed the most, just being in the locker room around my guys."

He also said facing head coach Ben Johnson and the team "was tough. Nobody wants to look someone in the eye after you've done something detrimental like that to the team, but those are things you have to do to move forward."

Sweat notched 10 sacks last season, which was the second-highest mark of his career. He finished with 12.5 during his one Pro Bowl season in 2023.

He had two sacks through the first five games of this season and will look to add to that total when the Bears face the Seattle Seahawks in a highly anticipated NFC showdown between potential contenders on Monday.

Javonte Carries Cowboys Back Into Race 😤

But he tore his ACL during a December matchup against the Denver Broncos, ending his season and calling into question when he would be able to return for the 2026 campaign.

The Packers could use him back. The team is tied for 15th in the NFL with 16 sacks on the season, though the pass defense has been solid in general (208 YPG, ninth in the NFL). Still, the team finds itself last in the loaded NFC North despite being 4-3 overall and has gone just 1-2 against its divisional rivals thus far.

Next week would make for a logical potential return point, at least to practice. Because the Packers play on Thursday night this week against the Carolina Panthers, they'll have a longer runway before a Week 9 contest against the New England Patriots. But the team also has a Week 11 bye, which means Parsons' return to game action might be delayed until Week 12.

"At the end of the day, that's the medical," LaFleur told reporters about how it will be decided to clear Parsons for practice. "I'm itching at it though, for sure."

articles.title: Kylie Kelce reveals strict parenting boundary involving Donna Kelce’s parents as she opens up about raising four daughters
articles.summary: Kylie Kelce has a clear approach to raising her four daughters, and it starts with respect for her parenting choices.
articles.body: Kylie Kelce has a clear approach to raising her four daughters, and it starts with respect for her parenting choices. The Not Gonna Lie podcast host recently opened up about setting boundaries with her and Jason Kelce’s parents, revealing that her family has largely made the experience easier. From protecting a newborn’s health to limiting what relatives could do around her children, Kylie explained why communication matters. Her comments also shed light on how the couple balances family relationships with their growing concerns about privacy and their daughters’ safety.Kylie Kelce reveals the boundaries she set with Jason Kelce’s parentsDuring a bonus segment of her Not Gonna Lie podcast, Kylie answered a listener’s question about whether she had ever needed to establish boundaries with the grandparents.Her answer focused on a simple request she made after welcoming her first daughter, Wyatt. Kylie asked relatives not to kiss the baby’s face, head or hands, and said they respected her wishes.“I asked people not to kiss her face or her head or her hands and everybody listened,” she said after thinking about the question for a brief moment. “We have a good little squad. Squad understands the assignment.”Kylie praised both sides of the family for understanding their role as grandparents without challenging her and Jason’s decisions as parents.“[Our] squad is very respectful about the fact that they have raised their grown children and that this is an opportunity for them to be fun, loving grandparents and supportive,” Kylie continued. “We actually made out like thieves on this one.”The couple faced another reason to be cautious when Wyatt was six months old and the COVID-19 pandemic began. Kylie said the uncertainty surrounding the virus led them to tighten precautions, particularly around travel.“Being the germaphobe that I am and also the unknown with a 6-month-old in your house, we locked it down pretty fast. We were very careful,” she explained. “That was the time where we set boundaries just in terms of like travel and things like that.”“But outside of that, not really,” she added, referring to boundary setting in her family. “Everyone understands the assignment. So, we really lucked out.”Why Kylie Kelce prioritises her daughters’ privacy and safetyKylie and Jason are parents to Wyatt, seven, Elliotte, five, Bennett, three, and Finnley, 18 months. Although they sometimes discuss family life publicly, Kylie has become more selective about sharing pictures of their daughters online.She previously explained that she no longer wanted to post their faces on social media, citing concerns about their safety and the permanence of online content.“I overall want to ensure my kids’ safety, and that’s always going to be the top priority.”Kylie has also considered how her daughters might feel when they grow older and discover years of personal moments preserved online. She wants them to have more control over their own digital lives.Her approach reflects a balance between welcoming family support and protecting her children’s boundaries. For Kylie, having relatives who listen has made that balance easier to maintain.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes vs. Tom Brady: Comparing the NFL legends’ impact on children through charity
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady have built careers defined by Super Bowl victories, record-breaking performances and immense success.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Tom Brady have built careers defined by Super Bowl victories, record-breaking performances and immense success. Yet their influence reaches far beyond the football field. Both NFL icons have used their platforms to support charitable causes, helping children and communities access opportunities that can shape their futures. Mahomes has focused much of his philanthropic work on youth development and education, while Brady has spent years raising money for inclusion programmes. Their approaches differ, but both show how a star athlete’s impact can extend well beyond game day.Patrick Mahomes’ charitable work puts children and education firstMahomes has made children's wellbeing a central part of his off-field work through the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation, which he established in 2019. The organisation supports initiatives focused on health, wellness and underserved communities, with an emphasis on giving young people better opportunities.One of his notable commitments came in 2023, when the foundation pledged $1.625 million to Boys & Girls Clubs of America through a multiyear partnership. The commitment also included $1,500 for every regular-season touchdown Mahomes recorded, linking his performance on the field to support for young people.His charitable efforts have also reached children in Kansas City through education programmes. In February 2025, local reporting highlighted his foundation's support for early education scholarships through the Systems of Care Initiative. The programme aimed to help families access educational opportunities during children's formative years.Mahomes and his wife, Brittany, have also used their annual charity gala to support a wider range of causes. Their sixth 15 and the Mahomies Gala raised $1,508,000 in October 2025 for more than 20 charities.These efforts reflect a broad approach to helping children. Rather than concentrating on one issue, Mahomes' foundation backs programmes that can support young people at different stages of life.Tom Brady’s charitable legacy supports inclusion and opportunityBrady's charitable work has followed a different path, with a longstanding focus on Best Buddies International. The organisation creates opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities through friendship programmes, employment support and leadership development.His involvement spans more than two decades. In November 2023, Best Buddies reported that Brady had helped raise more than $100 million for the organisation through his role as a global ambassador.That figure represents money he helped raise, not his personal donations. Still, it highlights the scale of his fundraising influence and the reach of his partnership with the charity.Best Buddies previously reported in 2017 that Brady's involvement had helped generate $46.5 million for the organisation. Six years later, the group honoured him with its Spirit of Leadership Award, recognising his continued support.While Mahomes has placed a strong emphasis on children's education and youth programmes, Brady's work has helped expand inclusion and opportunities for people with disabilities.Their charitable legacies measure success differently from their football records. articles.body: Travis Kelce continues to make an impact in Kansas City beyond the football field. The Kansas City Chiefs tight end has secured another $35,000 for Operation Breakthrough after winning Nationwide’s Charity Challenge, adding to years of support for the nonprofit. His latest victory also makes him the first player to win the fan-driven award three times in its 11-year history. With nearly $2 million in contributions to the organisation over the years, Kelce’s latest achievement highlights how his charitable work is helping children access educational opportunities and build skills that could shape their futures.Travis Kelce’s $35,000 award brings fresh support to Operation BreakthroughKelce’s latest charity win gives Operation Breakthrough additional funding to continue its work with children and families in the Kansas City area. The nonprofit focuses on helping young people from disadvantaged backgrounds by providing educational resources and opportunities they might otherwise struggle to access.Unlike a traditional award decided by a panel, Nationwide’s Charity Challenge relies on public participation. Fans vote for their preferred nominees through social media, with the winning player securing a donation for their chosen charitable organisation.Kelce’s victory reflects the strong support he continues to receive from Chiefs fans. It also adds another milestone to his relationship with Operation Breakthrough, which has received nearly $2 million from the tight end over the years.The $35,000 prize may be smaller than some of the contributions made by major philanthropists, but it provides another source of funding for programmes that can make a direct difference in children's lives. By allowing children to experiment, solve problems and develop technical skills, the lab helps introduce them to subjects that could influence their future education and career choices.Kelce’s latest award also continues a strong record for Kansas City players in Nationwide’s Charity Challenge. Chiefs stars have won the honour in five of the past 10 seasons. articles.summary: The New York Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, and the young quarterback has impressed under center so far.
articles.body:
The New York Giants traded for J.J. McCarthy after Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending injury, and the young quarterback has impressed under center so far.

But the Giants may have a problem on their hands, with two 23-year-old former first-round draft picks in their quarterback room. General manager Joe Schoen isn't concerned about a potential predicament.

"To have two young guys with Jaxson and J.J., both talented players, it's a good position to be in," Schoen told reporters . "It's a good position to be in."

As it stands now, Dart is more than likely still seen as the franchise quarterback. He had a strong rookie year in 2025, throwing for 2,272 yards, 15 touchdowns and five interceptions while rushing for 487 yards and nine touchdowns.

McCarthy has had a rough start to his career, but appears to be turning a corner in New York. In his Giants debut against the New Orleans Saints, he threw for 243 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter alone. Last week against the Houston Texans, he had 252 passing yards in an overtime win.

If McCarthy keeps playing at a high level, he could end up being a valuable trade asset for the Giants when Dart is back on the field next year. Until then, he'll look to keep proving that he's capable of being a starting quarterback.

articles.title: Mindblowing JSN stat highlights his elite play since start of 2025
articles.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has outperformed four NFL teams’ entire receiving corps in receiving yards recorded dating back to the start of last season.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has delivered an extraordinary run of production since the start of the 2025 NFL season, and his numbers have been so gargantuan that they've exceeded that of several teams' entire wide receiver rooms in that time.

According to BetMGM, Smith-Njigba has recorded more receiving yards and touchdowns than the Miami Dolphins ', New York Jets ', Las Vegas Raiders ' and Cleveland Browns ' entire wide receiver rooms dating back to the start of last season.

Smith-Njigba has accumulated 2,660 receiving yards and 18 REC touchdowns in that span, surpassing Miami's 2,602 REC yards and 15 REC TDs, New York's 2,585 yards and 16 TDs, Las Vegas' 2,461 yards and 15 TDs and Cleveland's 2,423 yards and seven TDs. JSN has outproduced each group individually, which highlights his remarkable consistency and importance to Seattle's offense.

Smith-Njigba recorded 1,793 receiving yards in 2025, and won the AP NFL Offensive Player of the Year award as a result. He has recorded 867 receiving yards thus far this season, continuing his exceptional production into the current year.

The feat is particularly impressive given the fact that the Dolphins and Jets have both had elite wide receivers on their teams for most or all of the stretch of time under the microscope. Miami had Jaylen Waddle last season, while the Jets have had Garrett Wilson leading there receiving unit throughout the entire stretch of time. Both receivers have established themselves as perennial 1,000-yard threats, making Smith-Njigba's accomplishment in surpassing those receiving corps even more remarkable.

Sunday morning football doesn't do the same numbers as Sunday afternoon or evening (or Monday night or Thursday) football, but it does better than anything else on TV at that time of day.

The Week 7 game between the Steelers and Saints averaged 7.7 million viewers , per ESPN.

The fourth straight Sunday morning game drew the third-highest audience for any international game on NFL Network.

The four European games played in October (three in London, one in France) averaged 7.1 million viewers on NFLN.

The only problem with early-morning football (which will proliferate if/when the NFL secures the ability to stage 16 international games per year) is that it renders the Sunday morning pregame shows irrelevant. As more and more games are played at 9:30 a.m. ET, the networks may reconsider whether they even want to have pregame shows.

That said, the networks televising Sunday afternoon games need a studio presence for updates and halftimes. But the noon ET to 1:00 p.m. ET pregame shows will get smaller and smaller audiences as more and more games are played on Sunday morning.

articles.title: Vikings Get Good Jonathan Taylor News via Colts’ Buckner Trade
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings are in prime position to make a trade for Jonathan Taylor of the Indianapolis Colts, but they may have to move fast. The post Vikings G...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings have not said they want to trade for a running back, let alone a high-end and expensive one like Jonathan Taylor — but the motive, means and opportunity all exist for the league's last undefeated team to make off with the three-time Pro Bowl RB in an NFL version of a blockbuster talent heist.

Indianapolis has signaled its position as perhaps the biggest sellers ahead of the trade deadline (November 10), moving fast and hard on Tuesday, October 27 on two deals that shipped recent Pro Bowlers to contenders.

First, the Colts sent eight-time Pro Bowl offensive guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks in exchange for a third-round pick in 2027 and a fifth-rounder in 2028. Just hours later, Indy shipped off three-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers for a fourth-round selection next year.

"Reunion! The Colts are trading three-time Pro Bowl DL DeForest Buckner to the 49ers for a 2027 fourth-round pick, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports," Tom Pelissero reported via X . "Buckner came to San Francisco as the No. 7 overall pick in the 2016 [draft]. A decade later, he's back."

Not only do the Colts' moves signal that essentially any player on the team is for sale at the right price, but that elite talent can be had at reasonable value.

Taylor's cost is likely to fall in the range of a second-round pick, which should prove more than worth it to the Vikings given that they are the sole undefeated team in the NFL, even despite the state of their offense.

Adding Elite Running Back Like Jonathan Taylor Best, Perhaps Only, Way for Vikings to Elevate Offense

All of this is good news for the Vikings if they intend to take a swing on a major offensive roster improvement.

The only logical way to achieve a jump on that side of the football is to slot in a top-10 running back. Dealing for a quarterback at this point probably doesn't change the facts on the ground in 2026, which all point to Kyler Murray being mediocre, at best.

That means the team will continue to get less than maximum possible production from an elite wide receiver Justin Jefferson who is suffering through another subpar year, at least by his standards, as he battles through QB purgatory.

Vikings Have Questions at RB Amid Injury to Aaron Jones Sr.

Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell told reporters Monday that he doesn't believe the team's RB room has a depth deficiency, even after Aaron Jones Sr. suffered a re-aggravation of an existing knee injury against the Colts on Sunday and could miss time moving forward.

"I feel good about the room, and we'll meet as a staff and get together with Nolan [Teasley] here and talk through that, what it looks like," O'Connell said . "But with where Aaron's at and [how] we feel coming out of the game, I don't necessarily see it as a depth issue at all. But obviously, things could change as we go day-to-day here."

Meanwhile, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reported that Minnesota is likely to get more serious about the trade market this week.

"The #Vikings are expected to 'further ramp up' conversations with teams on available players via trade this week, @alec_lewis mentioned via @AlecLewisShow," the VikingzFanPage wrote on X .

The Colts' actions have now set the stage for the Vikings to take the one Super Bowl swing they can via an offer for Taylor. The only question remaining is whether they're willing to make the move.

articles.title: Jaxon Smith-Njigba Announces Tragic Personal News After Seahawks’ Win vs. Chiefs
articles.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba makes personal announcement after the Seahawks' latest win. The post Jaxon Smith-Njigba Announces Tragic Personal News After Seahawks’ Win...
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba had himself another strong showing against the Kansas City Chiefs, but the playmaker appears to be playing with a heavy heart. After the primetime victory, Smith-Njigba hinted about a loss in the family.

The news comes as Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald alluded to Smith-Njigba playing through personal difficulties.

"(That) was for you nana!!!!" Smith-Njigba noted in an October 26, post to his Instagram Stories along with a photo. "I lovvveeee youuu.

Smith-Njigba posted nine receptions for 150 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. Macdonald continues to be impressed with Smith-Njigba, especially given the challenging circumstances.

"He's tremendous," Macdonald said of Smith-Njigba, per Yahoo Sports. "I don't know how else to describe him. He's had some adversity this week. Just going to leave it like that.

"But just really proud of him as a person. As a person, competitor, teammate, how do you not just have the most respect for the guy and love him for how he operates?"

Seahawks WR Jaxon Smith-Njigba Labeled as 'Potential Hall of Famer' by Nick Emmanwori

Smith-Njigba's play earned him a nomination for the NFL Air & Ground Player of the Week. Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori gushed over Smith-Njigba labeling the star as a "potential Hall of Famer."

"He's un-guardable. It's pretty amazing to see," Emmanwori noted on Smith-Njigba, per Seahawks.com's Ari Horton. "I'm sitting there thinking like, 'Wow, this (is a) potential Hall of Famer.' Great, great receiver.

"And knowing that he's getting double teamed and they're sending cloud his way and he's still making plays, it's crazy. It's like you can't even fathom it. So big ups to him. He's one of one."

Seahawks Star JSN Leads All NFL Receivers With 867 Yards & 8 Touchdowns

Through the first seven weeks of the NFL season, Smith-Njigba is leading all NFL receivers with 867 yards and eight touchdowns. Only Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride has more receptions (59) than JSN's 58 catches.

The good news for Seahawks fans is that the star signed a lucrative four-year, $168.6 million contract extension over the offseason. Smith-Njigba is under contract with Seattle through the 2031 season.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba Embraces His Family's African Roots

Aside from Smith-Njigba's social media post, little details have been revealed about the star's "Nana." We do know that Smith-Njigba has a close relationship with his family.

Smith-Njigba was born in Nacogdoches, Texas, but embraces his family's diverse roots which includes ties to Sierra Leon and Nigeria. The star's parents, Maada Smith-Njigba and Jami Smith, are often at Seahawks games cheering on the playmaker.

"You know, my grandfather came to the United States in the 70s," Smith-Njigba told reporters after the Seahawks' Super Bowl win. "Had to work for everything that he had. Brought a lot of people over here. Brought a lot of family over here, and he was a leader.

"And took pride in who he was and what he had to give back to, and I represent him. I represent my family. I represent Sierra Leone, Bo, Freetown. It's an honor just to even say that."

The Green Bay Packers fell to a 4-3 record after suffering a tough 20-17 Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions. Although many believe the club got a bit screwed over by some controversial officiating, head coach Matt LaFleur took it easy on NFL referees on Tuesday.

"I don't think officiating in this league is very easy," LaFleur said. "I really don't. I think things happen quickly, and there's some bang-bang decisions they have to make. So I don't think they have an easy job. All you want as a coach is consistency."

articles.title: Lakers starter opens up about changing shooting form, unique routine
articles.summary: Matisse Thybulle's changes have yielded positive results.
articles.body:
While Matisse Thybulle was playing for the Trail Blazers — the same team the Lakers hosted Tuesday night — he knew he needed to make a change to his shot.

The results have not only led to a strong shooting stretch to kick off his tenure as a Laker but also a unique pregame shooting routine that's paying off.

The eighth-year wing out of Washington has a unique twist to his pregame shooting routine: Thybulle cycles in "no-dip" 3s (when a player catches the pass and immediately shoots it from their chest or above their head without dropping the ball down around their waist) and one-handed 3s.

The origins of the No. 20 pick in the 2019 NBA Draft incorporating unorthodox shooting into his routine stems from working with Trail Blazers shooting coach John Townsend during 2024-25 as he was rehabbing from a preseason right knee surgery and sprained right ankle that sidelined him for the first 67 games that season.

"My shot has never been something I was confident in," Thybulle told the California Post on Tuesday. "It was always an insecurity of mine."

The most significant changes that were made to his shot: moving Thybulle's right (shooting) arm more to the side and keeping his elbow more tucked in.

Townsend had Thybulle go through "platform shooting" to accommodate him not being able to always jump as he rehabbed from the lower-body ailments.

"And then I started to notice some differences," Thybulle told The Post. "I was probably like a month out of being able to play again. And he's like, 'Well, you kind of have to decide now: Do you want to change your shot and stick to it and you can't go back? Or keep shooting the way you've been shooting?'

"I was like, 'But I want to change it.' So then we just decided to just stick with the changes that we were doing, trust the work and not really worry too much about the results for a little bit."

After shooting 34.6% on 3s in 2023-24, Thybulle shot 43.8% from deep across 15 regular-season games in 2024-25 (albeit on small volume — 21 of 48) and 39.8% in 30 games in 2025-26 (37 of 93).

He entered Tuesday shooting 46.7% on 3s (7 of 15).

"So far," Thybulle told The Post, "it's worked out."

The reason he incorporates the no-dip and one-handed 3s into his pregame routine is because it helps him maintain his shooting form.

"It was a huge foundational piece of just having my hand under the ball next to my head and then shooting through it," Thybulle said. "And it became something that we would go back to a lot if my shot started to float around or I wasn't shooting the way I wanted to. And then it just became a thing of like, well, 'Am I confident enough to shoot that in a game? Do I trust myself to shoot it?'"

The answer is yes, with Thybulle saying he took a "couple" of no-dip 3s with the Blazers last season.

He made his first no-dip 3 with the Lakers in the preseason during the Oct. 8 home win over the Kings.

And he made his first of the regular season during the third quarter of Sunday's road win over the Jazz.

"Having done it, I had gotten so many reps of it," Thybulle told The Post, "I got pretty confident in that being a good shot."

Thybulle's taken enough no-dip 3s that he doesn't consider it a unique shot.

"That's just a part of my shot archetype and shot package," he told The Post. "I actually prefer it at times."

Thybulle added: "There's less variables. When you catch a no-dip shot, you're under the ball, you have to fully extend. Whereas when you catch a regular pass, dip the ball down sometimes, you catch it across your body, you bring it over. Gotta make sure your legs are under you. There's just more pieces to it. Luka [Doncic ] and [ Austin Reaves ] throw such good passes that if I put my hands up, I'm literally catching it in my shooting pocket and I can just finish it through."

Even though he doesn't shoot the one-handed 3s in games, it's also an important part of staying true to his modified shooting form.

"A bad habit I have in mind is my elbow gets out from underneath the ball," Thybulle told The Post. "If you try to do that with one hand, you're going to drop the ball. You can't hold it. So it really forces you to be underneath the basketball. And then, you bring another hand and the carryover is really helpful."

For Thybulle, the unconventional forms are all about "laying the foundation" for his shot: physically and mentally.

"It takes a level of confidence and not caring to shoot those shots in public," he told The Post. "Because I'll shoot one-handed shots to this day and just airball them. It's the reason people shoot with two hands — it's a hard shot.

"For me, the willingness to shoot through those embarrassing moments and trust that this is something that helps me and can guide me to the way I want to shoot, that to me, more than anything … one part physical, another part mental. Just like getting that voice in your head that tells you like shoot the regular way so that you can make it. 'Cause if you do it this way, you might miss and it's going to be embarrassing. Just like free yourself of that and just like trust the process."

With the Minnesota Vikings (6-0) taking on the Detroit Lions (4-2) in Week 8 on Sunday, there is no denying that defensive coordinator Brian Flores will be looking to stop Jared Goff and the high-powered opposing offense. articles.title: Drake Maye and Dak Prescott expand their portfolios with an unexpected investment beyond their multimillion-dollar NFL careers
articles.summary: Drake Maye and Dak Prescott are getting more than endorsement money from their latest business move.
articles.body: Drake Maye and Dak Prescott are getting more than endorsement money from their latest business move. The New England Patriots and Dallas Cowboys quarterbacks have become athlete-owners of Athletic Brewing Company, adding an ownership stake to a deal that also requires them to promote its nonalcoholic beer. The partnership puts a young quarterback still learning the business world alongside a veteran who has spent years building interests outside football. Athletic Brewing has already established a sizable market presence, but the company has not disclosed the value of either player's stake.Drake Maye and Dak Prescott become owners of Athletic BrewingAthletic Brewing announced the multiyear partnerships in September 2026. Both quarterbacks will appear in the company's marketing, including its “Athletic Fits” campaign, but the ownership element gives the arrangement a different financial dimension. Rather than simply lending their names to a product, Maye and Prescott now have a stake in the business they are helping promote.The company has grown considerably since its commercial launch in 2018. It is now the largest dedicated nonalcoholic brewer in the United States, with products available at more than 75,000 retail locations and served at over 200 sports and entertainment venues. Athletic Brewing was valued at about $800 million after raising $50 million in an investment round in 2024.That scale gives the deal a clear appeal, although it does not guarantee a financial return. Athletic Brewing has not revealed how much either quarterback invested, what percentage they own or the current value of their individual stakes. Without those details, assigning a dollar figure to their holdings would be speculation.For Maye, the partnership also offers a chance to learn about entrepreneurship while he is still early in his professional career. The 24-year-old quarterback has spoken about wanting to understand business beyond the NFL. An ownership role gives him a closer look at how a company grows, reaches customers and builds a brand over time.Prescott brings more business experience to the partnershipPrescott's move into Athletic Brewing fits a wider pattern in his off-field activities. The 33-year-old Cowboys quarterback has built a portfolio of investments and partnerships during his NFL career. He is also an investor in Spindrift, the sparkling-water brand he used to drink before becoming involved with the company. His experience gives him a different starting point from Maye, who is only beginning to explore opportunities beyond football.The two quarterbacks are also taking different routes into the same venture. Maye can use the partnership to develop his business knowledge early, while Prescott adds another company to an existing collection of interests. Their shared involvement highlights how athlete partnerships can offer more than a fee for appearing in advertisements, provided the underlying business performs well.The commercial work remains part of the agreement. Maye's campaign spot begins with him throwing a football before shifting to a tailgate scene, while Prescott's advertisement centres on a backyard cookout. Athletic Brewing gains two established NFL names to help reach consumers, and the quarterbacks retain a financial interest in the company they promote.The key question is whether that ownership will eventually prove more valuable than a conventional endorsement deal. The company's growth offers a reason for optimism, but neither player's stake has been disclosed, and future returns remain uncertain. For now, the arrangement gives both quarterbacks a role beyond advertising.
